#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=lstmcogs
#   --time=48:00:00
#   --cpus-per-task=5
#   --ntasks-per-node=1
#   --nodes=1
#   --qos=high
#   --constrain=xeon-g6
#   --gres=gpu:volta:1
#   --array=0-9

#flux: --job-name=lstmcogs
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 5
#flux: --time-limit=48h

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:volta:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU (or without a Volta GPU), causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --array=0-9
# Flux job arrays are not available as a universally portable batch-script directive.
# Performance implication: you must submit multiple jobs manually; this can increase scheduler overhead and reduce throughput.

# Omitted Slurm option: --qos=high
# Flux QoS/priority mappings are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may have different priority/limits than intended, affecting wait time or eligibility.

# Omitted Slurm option: --constrain=xeon-g6
# Flux constraints/feature selection are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may land on different CPU microarchitecture, affecting performance or compatibility.

# Slurm variable $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID is not set under Flux.
# Accept task id as first argument (default 0).
TASK_ID=${1:-0}

lr=1.0
warmup_steps=4000
max_steps=8000
expname=LSTM

mkdir -p "$expname"
cd "$expname"

home="../../../"

i=$TASK_ID

python -u "$home"/main.py \
  --seed "$i" \
  --n_batch 128 \
  --n_layers 2 \
  --dim 512 \
  --lr "${lr}" \
  --temp 1.0 \
  --dropout 0.4 \
  --beam_size 5 \
  --gclip 5.0 \
  --accum_count 4 \
  --valid_steps 500 \
  --warmup_steps "${warmup_steps}" \
  --max_step "${max_steps}" \
  --tolarance 10 \
  --tb_dir "${expname}" \
  --COGS > "eval.$i.out" 2> "eval.$i.err"

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 Volta GPU (`--gres=gpu:volta:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.
The original Slurm job used an array (`--array=0-9`) but the Flux resource section does not provide an equivalent array mechanism; this changes the intended number of scheduled job instances.

The original Slurm job constrained placement via QoS and CPU constraint (`--qos=high`, `--constrain=xeon-g6`) but the Flux resource section has no equivalent constraints; scheduling eligibility and hardware characteristics may differ.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=lstmcogs
#SBATCH --time=48:00:00
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=5
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --qos=high
#SBATCH --constrain=xeon-g6
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:volta:1
#SBATCH --array=0-9

lr=1.0
warmup_steps=4000
max_steps=8000
expname=LSTM
mkdir -p $expname
cd $expname
home="../../../"
for i in `seq 0 9`
do
if [[ $i -eq $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID ]]; then
    python -u  $home/main.py \
    --seed $i \
    --n_batch 128 \
    --n_layers 2 \
    --dim 512 \
    --lr ${lr} \
    --temp 1.0 \
    --dropout 0.4 \
    --beam_size 5 \
    --gclip 5.0 \
    --accum_count 4 \
    --valid_steps 500 \
    --warmup_steps ${warmup_steps} \
    --max_step ${max_steps} \
    --tolarance 10 \
    --tb_dir ${expname} \
    --COGS > eval.$i.out 2> eval.$i.err
fi
done
